title: MI-32: Lean formalization of the parity and positive-polynomial upper bound
abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the MI-32 upper bound, that is, of the Latała-Świątkowski conjecture that for every regularity parameter alpha >= 1 there is a constant C > 0, independent of the dimension and of the entry laws, with E||X|| <= C (M(X) + D(X)) for every square random matrix X with independent mean-zero real entries whose absolute moments satisfy ||X_ij||_{L_2r} <= alpha ||X_ij||_{L_r} at every real order r >= 1. Here ||.|| is the Euclidean operator norm, M(X) is the sum of the largest row and column standard deviations, and D(X) is the max-min weak moment at order log(k+1) taken over one shared deterministic deletion set on both axes. The probability space is arbitrary and the subunit order log 2 at k = 1 is kept literally. The selected theorem MI32.main_upper carries a complete proof whose transitive axiom audit reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The proof runs through original-law positive-polynomial moments and interpolation, exact occupation-count localization, finite nets, a direct independent-coordinate Hilbert comparison, full original-law creator and annihilator contractions, positive vacuum iteration giving the local symmetric-law operator-moment theorem at the exact order log(n+1), a nested deterministic deletion decomposition with cubic two-sided variance screening, an elementary centered-Gram estimate for the far remainder, two two-shell block families controlled by the local theorem at scheduled orders, and the original-copy symmetrization reduction. Constants are explicit and conservative, not optimized.
